title: Deprecation & Transition Lanes: Practical migration guide for tokens, buttons, tables, charts
creator: Marisol Ortega
description: Create a practical, example-driven documentation page that codifies 'transition lanes' for deprecating legacy design tokens and component APIs (buttons, tables, charts). The goal is to give engineers and product teams a low-friction migration path: automated codemods where possible, explicit do/don't patterns, fallback compatibility shims, and a staged deprecation schedule tied to releases. This ticket covers content authoring, example code, migration checklist, and review cycles with Engineering and Product.
acceptance_criteria: A single docs page (and sub-anchors) exists in the design-system docs that outlines migration lanes for tokens, buttons, tables, and charts
At least three concrete code examples per component type showing legacy -> recommended usage and an explicit 'why this is better' note
Draft codemod scripts or clear pseudocode for automated token renames included (linked to ENG PR)
Review sign-off from Eng (E2E compatibility checks) and PM (deprecation schedule) recorded in comments
A migration checklist with rollback steps and recommended QA prompts is published
design_decisions: Favor additive API changes where possible: add new props with clear precedence rules rather than removing old ones immediately
Tokens: map legacy token names to semantic tokens in a curated mapping file; encourage semantic usage by showing cost/benefit and visual regressions
Charts: surface a compatibility layer that translates old config keys to new chart props for 2 releases before removing
Tables: provide a 'legacy-to-modern' prop shim that can be toggled at runtime for canary rollouts
Buttons: introduce size/variant tokens as aliases to old classes for one major release; new prop names are clearer and typed in the React API
migration_notes: Phase 0 (Docs + Warnings): Publish migration docs with lint rules that print warnings for legacy token usage
Phase 1 (Codemod): Offer codemod for token renames and prop replacements; target 80% automated migration coverage
Phase 2 (Compatibility Layer + Deprecation Window): Ship runtime compatibility shims for two minor releases with telemetry
Phase 3 (Removal): Remove legacy tokens and props after communications and 2 release cycles; provide rollback steps
Key stakeholders: Design (Marisol), Eng runtime (Priya Shah), Frontend infra (Ethan Kim), PM (Ravi Desai)
